[{"node":"permissions_menu_content","element":"menu_content","data":{},"elements":[{"node":"md_permissions_overview","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Overview","id":"permissions-overview","value":"# Roles & Permissions

> Identity — users, sessions, login, OAuth, CSRF — lives on the [Authentication](/authentication) page. This page is about **authorization**: what a signed-in user may do.

Loopar ships a role-based permission system with record-level ownership. It answers two separate questions on every request:

1. **Policy** — may this user run `Document:action` at all?
2. **Scope** — on which records? All of them, only the ones they own, or only their customer's?

A **grant** is a row of the `Permission` entity: `(relation, relation_name, document, action, scope, deny)`. `relation` is `Role` or `User`; `scope` is `all` (default), `own` or `customer`.

| Rule                                | Effect                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Grant first, ownership second       | Ownership never grants access by itself. The action grant is required; `own` only narrows it to the user's records. |
| Widest scope wins                   | If two grants cover the same cell (two roles, or role + user) and one is `all`, the result is `all`.                |
| Deny wins over everything           | A `deny` row on a user blocks the action even if a role grants `*:*`.                                               |
| `Administrator` bypasses everything | It is not a role; it is the built-in super user.                                                                    |

The check happens once per request in `AuthController.beforeAction`, before any document is loaded. Actions named `publicAction*` skip it entirely (public endpoints of the web workspace)."}},{"node":"md_permissions_base_roles","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Base roles","id":"permissions-base-roles","value":"## Base roles

Three system roles are seeded by the `loopar` app. **They grant entry, not data** — a user with only a base role sees an empty desk until an application role gives it documents.

| Role             | Grants      | Meant for                                                          |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `System Manager` | `*:*`       | Full access, like Administrator but a regular account              |
| `Desk User`      | `Profile:*` | Can log into the desk and manage their own profile                 |
| `Web User`       | —           | Portal / website accounts. Apps extend it with `own`-scoped grants |

System roles cannot be deleted (`is_system_role`); disable them instead."}},{"node":"md_permissions_app_roles","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Application roles","id":"permissions-app-roles","value":"## Application roles

Every installed app gets two roles **by convention**, seeded on install and on every update:

| Role            | Grants                                                   | Meaning                                                                                                    |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<App> Manager` | `App:<app>:*`                                            | Everything in the app, nothing else of the system                                                          |
| `<App> User`    | `App:<app>:view/list/search` (all) + `App:<app>:*` (own) | Reads everything in the app, creates and edits only its own records — so selects and catalogs keep working |

From there the admin narrows or widens per document in the Permission Manager.

### Declaring roles in your installer

```js
// apps/<app>/installer.js
import { CoreInstaller } from 'loopar';

export default class installer extends CoreInstaller {
  static roles = [
    {
      name: 'Sales Manager',               // same name as a default → replaces it
      description: 'Owner of the sales app',
      grants: [{ document: 'App:sales', action: '*' }],
    },
    {
      name: 'Web User',                    // extends a base role from another app
      grants: [
        { document: 'Quote', action: 'view', scope: 'own' },
        { document: 'Quote', action: 'list', scope: 'own' },
      ],
    },
  ];

  // static defaultRoles = false;          // opt out of the <App> Manager / User convention
}
```

A grant is `{ document, action, scope = 'all', deny = 0 }`. Seeding is idempotent: it only inserts what is missing and never rewrites what an admin changed. **Reset to defaults** in the Permission Manager drops every grant of a role and seeds the declared ones again."}},{"node":"md_permissions_grants","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Grants","id":"permissions-grants","value":"## Grant forms

`document` accepts several shapes, resolved from the most specific to the widest:

| `document`      | `action`        | Covers                                                                   |
| --------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Invoice`       | `update`        | one action of one document                                               |
| `Invoice`       | `*`             | every action of one document                                             |
| `*`             | `list`          | one action on every document                                             |
| `*`             | `*`             | everything (System Manager)                                              |
| `App:sales`    | `*` or `update` | every document of the `sales` app — including entities added later      |
| `Module:sales` | `view`          | explicit sidebar override (normally not needed, see *Module visibility*) |

`action` is the controller method without its prefix: `actionUpdate` → `update`, `publicActionSubmit` → `submit`. Custom actions of a controller are listed under **Custom** in the manager.

Two built-in actions deserve a mention:

| Action | Grants |
|--------|--------|
| `transition` | Running [workflow](/workflows) transitions. The workflow then narrows it per transition (allowed roles) |
| `print` | The printable view of a record. Previewing a Print Format needs `print` with scope `all` on its entity |

### Scope

| `scope` | Meaning                    |
| ------- | -------------------------- |
| `all`   | any record                 |
| `own`   | only records the user owns |
| `customer` | only records of the user's customer(s) — for portal users (see below) |

### Deny

A `deny` row (`relation = User`) blocks one action for one user regardless of roles. Unchecking an inherited cell in the manager creates it; checking it again removes it."}},{"node":"md_permissions_ownership","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Ownership","id":"permissions-ownership","value":"## Ownership (`scope: own`)

Every auditable entity carries a framework column **`__created_by__`**: the username that created the row, stamped on insert, ignored if sent in a payload, immutable afterwards. It sits next to `__created_at__` and never appears in forms.

When a grant is `own`, Loopar evaluates ownership **only for the request itself** — the `(document, action, name)` the controller was called with:

* **Single record** (`view`, `update`, `delete`, `bulkDelete`, custom actions with a `name`): checked in `beforeAction` with one lightweight read. Not the owner → `403`.
* **Lists** (`list`, selects' `search`, any action that lists the requested document): the model injects `__created_by__ = <user>` into the query, so rows *and* pagination count match.
* **Anything a controller loads internally** (`Invoice.update` reading `Material`s) is never narrowed: the scope is bound to the request, not to `getDocument`. Use `loopar.getList(doc, { unscoped: true })` when server code must list everything.

### When the owner is not the creator

Override the resolution in the controller:

```js
export default class QuoteController extends BaseController {
  // simplest: another column identifies the owner
  static ownerField = 'customer';

  // or compound rules
  async isOwner(name, user) { /* true | false | null (record missing → 404) */ }
  async ownerCondition(user) { return { customer: { [Op.in]: await this.#customersOf(user) } }; }
}
```

Records created before the upgrade have `__created_by__ = NULL`: nobody owns them, only `all` grants reach them.

## Customer scope (`scope: customer`)

Portal users — a customer's people signing in to see *their* orders, invoices or tickets — are not owners of those records: staff created them. The `customer` scope narrows a grant to the records of the user's customer(s), through one explicit chain set up by staff:

```
User ──(Customer Contact.user)──▶ Customer Contact ──(Customer.contacts)──▶ Customer(s)
```

Records an app exposes to customers carry a `customer` field (a link to [Customer](/crm)). A grant with scope `customer` then filters lists and checks single records against that field — never by matching emails, never from a name sent by the client.

| Scope ranking | Widest wins: `own` < `customer` < `all` |
|---|---|

Server code reads the identity with `portalIdentity()` (`{ user, contact, customers }`) or `requirePortalIdentity()` (401/403 when not signed in or not linked). Desk figures (number cards, dashboards) ignore `customer` grants — they are for staff.
"}},{"node":"md_permissions_modules","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Module visibility","id":"permissions-modules","value":"## Module visibility

The desk sidebar and the module pages are **derived from document grants** — no navigation grants to maintain:

* A module is visible when the user can `list` or `view` at least one document in it (or holds an explicit `Module:<name> view`).
* Inside a module, only the documents the user can reach are shown, and the counter follows.

So `Sales Manager` (`App:sales:*`) sees the *sales* group with every entity and page of the app, and nothing else."}},{"node":"md_permissions_manager","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Permission Manager","id":"permissions-manager","value":"## Permission Manager

Desk → Auth → **Role Permission Manager**.

* **Left rail** — every subject: roles grouped by *System*, one section per app, *Custom*; then *Users*. Search on top.
* **Header** — the selected subject. For a user, its roles as chips (click to assign), the number of direct overrides and **Clear overrides**; for an app role, **Reset to defaults**.
* **App tabs** — one grid per app.
* **Whole app row** — the `App:<app>` grant. `+ All` creates `App:<app>:*`; a single cell creates `App:<app>:<action>`.
* **Cells** —

| Look               | Meaning                                                                                                   |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| solid check        | direct grant on this subject                                                                              |
| dashed check       | inherited: from a wildcard (`Doc:*`, `App:x`, `*:x`) or, for a user, from a role — hover shows the source |
| amber, person icon | scope `own`                                                                                               |
| red ✕              | denied for this user                                                                                      |
| —                  | the action does not exist on that document                                                                |

Click toggles the grant; the small pill under a direct cell switches `all` / `own`. Unchecking a cell covered by a wildcard splits that wildcard into finer grants so the other cells keep what they had (`*:*` is refused — remove it explicitly)."}},{"node":"md_permissions_client","element":"markdown","data":{"label":"Client helpers","id":"permissions-client","value":"## Client helpers

The desk client receives the user's effective grants (app-level grants already expanded per document). From `@context/AuthContext`:

```jsx
import { useAuth } from '@context/AuthContext';

const { award, scope, canOn } = useAuth();

award('Invoice', 'update');                 // boolean — may run it at all
scope('Invoice', 'update');                 // 'all' | 'own' | null
canOn('Invoice', 'update', row);            // for THIS row (uses row.__created_by__)
canOn('Quote', 'update', row, { ownerField: 'customer' });
```

List rows carry `__created_by__` (not as a visible column) so `canOn` can decide per row. These helpers are cosmetic — hide or disable buttons — the server remains the source of truth.
"}}]}]
